scope: Broaden current DWG/DXF 3D peer research to parser robustness, silent writer loss, versioned ACIS/AcDs support boundaries, and implementation-ready local validation updates.

method.kind: Read-only review of public release notes, source documentation, and issue/PR histories, reconciled against current plan gates
method.evidenceRule: Release notes and issue/PR histories are route/failure-mode evidence only. Do not infer current peer behavior from an older issue; any execution comparison needs an exact release/commit, license, runtime, locally generated controls, and per-source disposition. ODA v5.4.1 remains authoritative for DWG layouts.

evidence.topic: LibreDWG current robustness and version boundary signals
observed: LibreDWG 0.14.1 release notes report an oversized 3DSOLID SAT block-size overflow fix and an off-by-one fix that had dropped the final SAT block during DXF export.
The same NEWS file says direct R2007 DWG encoding is not supported and falls back to R2010 encoding.
LibreDWG source documentation uses stable/unstable/unhandled/test-coverage categories and lists BODY, MESH, and associated 3D routes among its documented test-coverage gaps.
doesNotEstablish: that libdxfrw has the same defect
a normative DWG or ACIS byte layout
that LibreDWG has no tests beyond the documented inventory
evidence.planUse: Prioritize tiny boundary tests at changed ACIS chunk/length code and keep modern DWG writer claims version-specific. Use ODA v5.4.1 and this repository's generated tests, not peer implementation details, as authority.

evidence.topic: ACadSharp Prototype_1b issue history reconciled with released fix
observed: v3.6.51 notes report reading ACIS payloads for 3DSOLID, REGION, and BODY from DXF/DWG and reading the AcDs payload-area offset.
v3.6.51 notes include the full Prototype_1b section parser PR #1154; issue #1152 was closed as completed through that PR.
GitHub currently lists v3.8.0 as the latest ACadSharp release.
doesNotEstablish: full arbitrary-schema correctness of the parser
B-rep semantics, broad producer/version coverage, or current runtime behavior
a reason to retain the closed issue as an unresolved peer defect
evidence.planUse: Use the exact selected release, not pre-fix issue discussion, for any optional comparator; continue validating our own ODA-based AcDs linkage and schema boundaries independently.

evidence.topic: DXF writer silent-loss and numeric round-trip reports
observed: Open issue #1195 reports that ACadSharp 3.4.9 omitted DWG 3DSOLID/REGION entities from DXF without diagnostics; this report predates listed v3.8.0 and has not been reproduced in this review.
MESH DXF writer issue #1038 was closed by #1067, demonstrating a peer-reported mesh-to-proxy/empty-output failure mode and a linked fix.
ASCII DXF numeric precision issue #1179 was closed by #1186; v3.7.16 release notes record decimal-precision support.
doesNotEstablish: that the current ACadSharp release still loses solids or meshes
a need for textual byte identity across DXF producers
evidence.planUse: Strengthen existing writer-loss tests to match source entities to exact output/read-back disposition by identity and owner/block path; compare typed numeric semantics using declared tolerances, separately from opaque byte identity.

observed: HOOPS Exchange documents SAT/SAB B-rep access and explicitly excludes some advanced procedural ACIS geometries; surface/curve evaluators have different robustness levels.
Its format matrix treats tessellation and B-rep as separate support dimensions.
doesNotEstablish: that a runtime, license, or exact semantic result is available in this environment
evidence.planUse: Retain as an optional independent semantic route only; require exact pinned runtime and analytic validation, not tessellation or bounds as B-rep evidence.

nextActions: At changed ACIS carrier boundaries, add focused generated tests for empty/one/multiple/final chunks, bounded length, overflow arithmetic, truncation, and following-record alignment.
For the existing ACIS writer-loss gate, account for each source entity by identity and block/owner path and require exact retention or an explicit actionable failure/skip result.
For typed 3D values, validate strict read-back with explicit absolute/relative tolerances; keep exact opaque-byte digests as a separate assertion.
At the existing composed peer checkpoint only, use an exact current release/commit and local controls; if unavailable, record NOT_RUN and continue.
